newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BBL raises Belgian Bekaert to 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: BBL raises Belgian Bekaert to 'buy'.

text.p: An expected strong rise in profits at Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV rates the share a 'buy' from a previous 'hold', Belgium's Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) said.

"In 1997 and 1998, better prices, lower financial costs, productivity improvements and stabilised depreciation will lead to a strong upturn in profitability," BBL analyst Jean-Marie Caucheteux said in a research note.

"We anticipate operating margin - 7.5 percent in 1994 and 4.9 percent in 1996 - to peak at 7.9 percent, a record for Bekaert, in 1998," said Caucheteux. "Earnings should grow by 44 percent in 1997 and a further 16 percent in 1998."
He said 1996 will be a difficult year with current profit down 27 percent on 1995.
He expected a cyclical rebound in 1997 and 1998. "We are convinced that the bulk of the negative effect is over and the way is now clear for a more serene appraisal of the stock."
Bekaert is world leader in tyre cord making with a 22 percent market share.
BBL's research note was written when the stock was at 22,200 francs. BBL set a 12-month target of 25,000 francs.
At the end of Thursday morning Bekaert shares were down 25 francs at 24,125.
